paragraphs: Pasta e fagioli is an Italian family of pasta-and-bean soups whose regional forms vary; mashed beans and pasta starch give this tomato-tinged version its characteristic creamy body without dairy.

Pasta e fagioli simply means pasta and beans. It is Italian cucina povera—resourceful regional cooking with versions that may be brothy or nearly spoon-standing, white or tomato-tinted, vegetarian or enriched with pork. This pantry version leads with the familiar English description while keeping its proper name, and uses mashed beans rather than cream for its characteristic body. paragraphs: Italian wedding soup is an Italian American dish whose name refers to the pleasing marriage of meat and greens, not a prescribed wedding menu; tiny meatballs, broth, pasta, and escarole define the familiar form.

Italian wedding soup is not named for a wedding ceremony. The English name comes from minestra maritata, a 'married soup' describing the pleasing union of greens, broth, and meat. Italian-American versions made mini meatballs and tiny pasta especially familiar. This version keeps those beloved cues while returning escarole to equal billing with the meatballs.
